title: Sqrt(x)
statement_short: Given a non-negative integer x, return the square root of x rounded down to the nearest integer. The returned integer should be non-negative as well. Do not use any built-in exponent function or operator.
hint: Bounded integer range allows binary searching the answer range [0, x] for the largest integer k where k\*k <= x.
keywords: rounded down to the nearest integer
why_not: Right: Binary Search on Answer halves the search space [0, x] to find floor(sqrt(x)) in O(log x) time and O(1) space. Not Math / Geometry: Newton method works in O(log x) time, but binary search on the answer range is the standard pattern. Not Two Pointers: Linear scanning from 1 up to sqrt(x) takes O(sqrt(x)) time, which is slower than logarithmic binary search. Not 1D DP: Dynamic programming state caching does not apply to numerical square root search.
